title: Ang 53–71: the ashtpadis
hookLine: longer hymns, including truth and truthful living on ang 62
tomorrow: what if a whole life fit inside one night?

cards: Everything gets ranked now: top ten lists, five stars, best of the year. Ask people to rank what matters in a person and honesty usually lands somewhere near the top. So here's an odd line to find on ang 62.
Guru Nanak puts truth above everything. Then, in the very next breath, he names something higher than truth. What could possibly outrank it?

teach.b: From ang 53 to 71, Sri Rag slows down. These are ashtpadis: longer hymns that take their time with one theme.

teach.h: TRUTH ABOVE ALL, TRUTHFUL LIVING HIGHER.
teach.b: In the middle of them, on ang 62, Guru Nanak writes, in paraphrase: truth is higher than everything; higher still is truthful living.
In his words, sach, truth, and above it, sach aachaar: truth as conduct, truth as the way you actually behave. So the puzzle solves itself once you hear the second word. Nothing beats truth.
But truth you only know sits lower than truth you do. A person can be right about everything and still live false: correct in every argument, careless at the counter.
And in the Granth, sach isn't only a fact being accurate.

teach.h: SACH: ALSO A NAME FOR THE ONE.
teach.b: It's also a name for the One, the True. So truthful living isn't just not lying.

It's letting what's most real steer your hands: how you earn, how you speak about someone who isn't in the room, what you do when the mistake is in your favor. That's why the line belongs in a long hymn.
A slogan can tell you truth matters. It takes a hymn that circles and circles to show truth getting into the small parts of a day.

how: Sikhs often quote the ang 62 line on truth and truthful living as a summary of the Sikh way: belief carried into honest work, honest speech and fair dealing.

games.q: at a family party your uncle wins a long argument about honesty, then pockets extra change a cashier handed him by mistake. what would ang 62 say about his evening?
o: he was right in the argument, so he's on the side of truth.
truth lived ranks higher than winning the argument about it.
the cashier made the mistake, so truth isn't really involved.
games.why: truth known is high; truthful living is higher. being right in the argument doesn't reach the counter.

practice: If a Gurbani app is near, read ang 62 first, slowly. Take a pen and any scrap of paper and write two short lines by hand. On top, one thing you know is true.
Underneath it, one small way that truth could show up in what you do. Then set the pen down and stay with the second line, the higher one.
